text: Suppose A, B ∈ Mₙ(F) satisfy AB = Iₙ. Which conclusion is correct?
choices: BA = Iₙ automatically: a one-sided inverse of a square matrix is two-sided
BA = Iₙ only when A is also assumed invertible
BA can differ from Iₙ, just as for linear maps on infinite-dimensional spaces
BA = Iₙ holds over ℝ and ℂ but can fail over finite fields
explanation: AB = I makes L_B injective (Bx = 0 ⇒ x = ABx = 0), so by rank–nullity B is invertible, and A = (AB)B⁻¹ = B⁻¹, giving BA = I. Finite-dimensionality is essential: on F[x] the composition (d/dx) ∘ (integration) is the identity, but the reverse composition kills constants.
